source_text: Praecepta autem, quibus pietas fides iustitia sanctitas continetur, non solum non cessaverunt, verum etiam cumulata sunt. Et haec lex iustitiae in iudiciis custodiendae, quam de Deuteronomio protulimus, non ad cerimoniarum aetatem, sed ad praeceptorum perennitatem respicit nec cum circumcisione discessit, sed cum iustitia perseverat.
pass_a_gloss: But the precepts by which piety, faith, justice, holiness is contained have not only not ceased but have even been heaped up. And this law of justice to be kept in judgments, which we have brought forth from Deuteronomy, looks not to the age of ceremonies but to the perenniality of precepts, and did not depart with circumcision but perseveres with justice.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: The commands containing devotion, faith, justice, and holiness, however, not only did not cease; they were increased. This law about maintaining justice in judgments, which we quoted from Deuteronomy, concerns the enduring character of commands, not the temporary age of ceremonies. It did not disappear with circumcision; it continues with justice (Deuteronomy 24:16).

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the explicit argument from the law forbidding punishment of parents and children for one another’s sins.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
